title: India's 10-year bond heads for first weekly gain in 11 weeks, set to end record losing run - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
A Treasury rally helped Indian government bonds extend gains on Friday, ​putting the benchmark 10-year bond on course for its first weekly ‌rise in 11 weeksand ending its longest losing streak ​on record.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield ⁠traded slightly below Thursday’s levels at 7.3837%. It has eased over 9 bps so far this week, after gaining more than 70 ‌basis points in previous 10 straight weeks, a streak not seen since at least 1998, the earliest ‌data available on LSEG.

Investors ⁠lapped up Indian bonds this week, after ⁠the 10-year yield twice approached but did not breach the pivotal upside level of 7.50%, making prices attractive for entry.

Mutual funds emerged as the ​biggest value buyers, lapping ‌up about 40 billion rupees of bonds this week through Thursday.

The market also drew support from a slightly dovish Federal Reserve policy.

The Fed held rates steady in October, ‌with fewer hawkish dissents than expected, and Chair Kevin ​Warsh struck a less hawkish tone than markets had anticipated.

US midterm elections will be the next ⁠key focus, traders said, adding that their impact on war-related decisions and oil prices could have a bearing on debt ‌markets across the globe.

Americans will vote in midterm elections on Tuesday for control of the US Congress.

“If democrats are able to take over both the houses there will be some rally in the market, but if it’s a divided reaction, markets may remain subdued,” said Kruti Chheta, ‌fund manager at Mirae Asset Mutual Fund.

Demand at New Delhi’s 330 billion-rupee ($3.47 ​billion) debt sale will be key in sustaining this rally, a private bank trader said.

The overnight indexed ⁠swap curve flattened this week, as short-term rates surged faster amid ⁠tightening liquidity.

Rates have risen 2 to 10 bps so far this week.

The one-year OIS was ‌flat at 6.68% on Friday, the two-year rate was slightly down at 6.72%, and the five-year rate fell 1.25 ​bps to 6.8375%.
